claim: The Chennai Flood Monitor (RTFF & SDSS) GeoServer enumerated 344 feature-type layers on 2026-09-29, of which 343 answered anonymous WFS requests and 1 was auth-walled; a live re-census on 2026-10-03 returned 344 = 344 with no layers added or removed.
source: Desk census of the live GeoServer (GetCapabilities parse, single-day pull 2026-09-29; re-census 2026-10-03)
notes: Primary artifact: GetCapabilities census, reproducible via the command in DATA-CATALOGUE.md §6. Underpins the "open by accident, not by policy" finding (REPORT F1): no license, no API docs, no data policy anywhere on the portal. Upgrade to L4 not needed for the count itself; the policy-absence claim is a separate documented absence.

claim: On the flagship 38-station rain panel, 22 of 38 stations showed fresh data on census day 2026-09-29; on re-probe at ~08:00 IST 2026-10-04 only 10 of 38 (26%) carried a same-day reading, and 10 further stations had stopped together at the same minute (2026-09-29 16:30) — a pipeline/ingest failure signature left unfixed for five days.
source: Desk live probes of GetRainfallDatafordashboard, all 5 districts (2026-09-29 dashboard dump vs 2026-10-04 re-probe)
notes: Two captures five days apart via the same dashboard endpoint (per-district GetRainfallDatafordashboard). Same-source chain, so corroboration is partial; the batch-stop timestamp is the falsifiable core. Upgrade path: TNSDMA/WRD or station-vendor explanation of the 16:30 stop, or an independent IMD feed for the same stations. At NEM 2026 onset the panel's live coverage is 26%.

claim: Eight stations on the flagship panel — including the IMD reference gauge Nungambakkam — have served no new reading since 2025-05-10 (desk probe tally: 511 days as of 2026-10-04); three more are frozen at ~710 days (Mahabalipuram, VIT_CHENNAI, RANIPET) and RIMC Lab at 712 days.
notes: Frozen cohort unchanged between the 2026-09-29 census and the 2026-10-04 probe — "has not moved by a single reading". Nungambakkam is Chennai's historic IMD yardstick used in every flood comparison since 2015. Same-source chain; upgrade needs IMD's own record of the gauge or a second independent pipeline. A match in our mirror is a station record, not a finding about any person.

claim: Two panel stations (Mamallapuram AWS, Pallipattu AWS) served readings dated exactly 2025-10-04 when probed on 2026-10-04 — year-old data presented as current on a "real-time" dashboard.
notes: The annual-fossil pattern repeats across probes; it means the panel renders stale rows as live data, so "station present" must never be read as "station reporting". Verify by re-pulling on the anniversary pattern at the next probe.

claim: The public ward-level inundation table (ward_waterdepth_minmax) carries all 200 wards stamped 2021-08-11: the street-level "forecast" exposed as a data layer is a static five-monsoon-old scenario, not live model output.
source: Layer property inspection in the desk mirror (2026-09-29 pull; chennaidss-gis-layers on Hugging Face)
notes: REPORT F4. The live street-flood output exists only as image-only bulletin PDF maps during activations. This is the layer underpinning press claims of "street-level inundation alerts" — see cross-checks in MEDIA-CLAIMS.md entries 7, 11. Upgrade: if TNSDMA publishes a live ward-depth feed, the claim should be re-dated and re-levelled.

claim: The machine-readable ARG/AWS rain transaction layer tops out at 2022-09-06 (bulk 2018–2021, three straggler rows in 2022) while the dashboard API returns 2026 readings through a different pipeline: the open feed and the operational feed are not the same data path.
source: Desk mirror of aws_arg_full transaction table vs dashboard API payloads (2026-09-29)
notes: REPORT F3; per-year DuckDB group-by in the release archive. Even a diligent citizen reading the open feed gets a four-year-stale city. Upgrade path: TNSDMA statement on the pipeline split, or WRD documentation of the ingest architecture.

claim: The public alert endpoint GetPublishAlert has returned zero rows on every check to date; the portal publishes no API, RSS or SMS specification for alerts, and the host returns HTTP 403 to clients that do not carry the front-end's session cookie (re-confirmed 2026-10-04).
source: Desk API checks (0 rows on 2026-09-29 and prior) + direct fetch attempt 2026-10-04 (HTTP 403 to session-less client)
notes: REPORT F6. Empty feed + no spec = alert equity depends on having the right app installed and open (TN-Alert has no public spec either). The 403 is a source-access quirk, registered in the source registry — any future empty-feed check must use the scripted-session path, not a plain fetcher. First non-empty response during NEM 2026 is a beat event.

claim: During the Ditwah remnant (30 Nov–6 Dec 2025), the system's own data recorded the flood in three layers — a citizen level-6 severity report at the Puzhal surplus outflow (2025-12-04 03:00Z), bridge danger-level peaks the same day (Aminjikarai 7.705 m at 15:30; Manali 2.501 m), and 168 crowd reports in Nov 2025 — consistent with The Hindu's contemporaneous Ennore/Red Hills reporting (56 cm over 3 days; Red Hills shutters opened a sixth time).
source: Desk mirror layers (crowdsourced_173, AWLR bridge series) + The Hindu 2025-12-03
notes: REPORT F8. Two chains: (1) captured artifacts in the mirror (crowd + AWLR layers); (2) dated press (The Hindu, 2025-12-03). Caveat kept in the ledger: the two sensor/crowd layers are same-origin; the independent chain is the press. The system demonstrably worked as a recorder; whether it worked as a forecaster is unanswerable (no forecast archive — separate claim).

claim: Seven image-only PDF bulletins, all from the October 2025 activation, are the system's complete public output record; the model-run and bulletin archive stops at 2025-12-02 — before the Ditwah-remnant peak of 3–5 Dec 2025 — and no bulletin has been published since.
source: Desk mirror (chennai-flood-bulletins dataset; model-run registry layer inspection)
notes: Merges REPORT appendix rows 9 and 26 + catalogue gap G7. No forecast archive means no forecast-vs-observed comparison is possible (REPORT F5): after ₹107.2 crore, "how good is it?" has no public answer. The mirror holds the observed side; the forecast side must be captured per activation going forward.

claim: In the World Bank's own procurement annexes for P179189 (TNCRUDP), three Chennai RTFF contracts stand at US$0.00 disbursed with status "Pending Implementation": IN-TNUIFSL-350974-GO-RFB (RTDAS + flood control rooms, US$6.06M; bid opening trail 2023-03-20 → 2023-11-15 → 2024-09-10; footnoted "under TNSUDP. Agreement is yet to be executed"), IN-TNUIFSL-351017-CS-CDS (handholding supervision, US$83K; revised completion 2025-10-15 — a week before the "fully operational" launch) and IN-TNUIFSL-385194-CS-CDS (DEM/DSM, US$360K; revised 2024-08-30).
source: World Bank P179189 procurement plan annexes (Dec-2024 and Jun-2026), archived in docs/wb/
notes: Borrower-submitted, Bank-reviewed procurement annexes — official records, archived locally with .txt extractions; same facts repeat in the Jun-2026 plan (docs/wb/more/PP_2026-06-10.pdf). Both plans are same-publisher, so this is one chain, not two: upgrade to L4 needs TNUIFSL/GoTN-side confirmation (RTI on contract status). Read with the launch: the state launched on its own money while every Bank-side contract sat at zero disbursement.

claim: The August 2026 TNCRUDP procurement plan drops all four RTFF/storm-water-drainage contract lines while the June 2026 plan still listed them as "Pending Implementation" at $0.00 disbursed — with no public cancellation or descope note anywhere.
source: World Bank P179189 procurement plans, Jun-2026 vs Aug-2026 (STEP-updated, base 2025-06-20), archived in docs/wb/more/
notes: Sharpest single open question the Bank's own paper raises: cancelled, absorbed, or re-funded elsewhere — nothing public says which. Same-publisher pair (Jun vs Aug 2026 plan); upgrade to L4 via RTI to TNUIFSL/WRD or a tender-portal sighting of a replacement/re-tender. Desk question to put to the World Bank PIC in writing.

claim: Across the 14 archived World Bank project documents for P179189 (PAD, IFSA, ESCP, launch brief, ISR Seq 1–4, audit TOR, two audit reports, three procurement plans), no document mentions flood forecasting or RTFF & SDSS in any results narrative: the PAD cites floods 25 times as rationale and never names the project; the DLI results framework contains no forecast-accuracy, uptime or alert indicator; and the fiduciary audit scope contains zero flood references.
source: 14 WB documents archived 2026-10-04 in docs/wb/more/ + ISR Seq 5 and both procurement plans in docs/wb/
notes: Documented absence inside our archive — completeness is bounded by what the Bank's WDS API exposes for the project, so the claim is "no public document in the disclosed set". The Loan/Financing Agreement (IBRD-96250) is not yet disclosed; when it appears it must be checked before this claim is treated as complete. Silence is program-long, not an ISR-Seq-5 quirk.

claim: Tamil Nadu government statements and press coverage report the RTFF & SDSS as India's first fully operational urban flood-forecasting decision-support system, sanctioned at ₹107.2 crore, covering 4,974 km² across five districts, operational since 22 October 2025; no sanction order, contract split or O&M budget for it is public.
source: The Hindu 2025-10-22 + syndicated launch coverage + CFM-DSS AboutUs page
notes: Documented but unauthenticated: one press-handout chain syndicated across outlets (MEDIA-CLAIMS P4 — entries 1–13 repeat the same fact sheet near-verbatim), plus the portal's own AboutUs. The "first in India" and "fully operational" framings are claims, not verified facts — no bulletin archive exists to test them (see ledgered claim on the 7-bulletin record). Upgrade path: GoTN sanction order via RTI (WRD/TNUIFSL), PDGF utilisation certificate.

claim: The project's cost was reported as ₹71 crore in November 2022 (sensor-expansion phase) and ₹107.2 crore at the October 2025 launch — a 51% rise in three years — and no public sanction order, revision note or audit trail explains the increase.
source: New Indian Express 2022-11-02 vs Oct-2025 launch coverage
notes: Two dated, independent press datapoints (New Indian Express 2022-11-02; launch coverage 2025-10), but both unauthenticated against primary financial records — hence L2, not L4: the corroborated fact is that two press figures disagree by 51%, not what the state actually sanctioned. Upgrade path: RTI for sanction orders + CAG report scan (registered source). REPORT appendix row 22; ELI10.md §2A.

claim: On 2 October 2026, Revenue & Disaster Management Secretary B. Chandramohan announced a new Integrated Flood Management Centre (IFMC) that "will predict street-level flooding three days before the actual flooding" — restating, one year later, the same street-level 72-hour promise made for RTFF & SDSS at its October 2025 launch, with no published document distinguishing IFMC from RTFF & SDSS.
notes: MEDIA-CLAIMS entry 22 (T5 re-announcement). Announcement recorded with URL + headline in the register but the article is not yet archived locally — fetch, save, hash to reach L3. Named subject: right of reply REQUIRED before any publication. Either an upgrade or a rebrand of the 2025 promise — the desk's IFMC watch (MEDIA-CLAIMS update protocol #3) tracks which. Cross-checks: ward layer static 2021; no forecast archive.

claim: In the mirrored station registries, AMC/sensor-vendor name fields are blank across all rows, and while 66 stations carry an active AMC flag, expiry dates (amcvalidtill) are populated for only about six — the annual-maintenance calendar for the flagship sensor network is not knowable from the system's own registry.
source: Desk registry scan of the 33 station-registry tables in the mirror (chennai-flood-monitor-transactions, HF)
notes: REPORT F10 + appendix rows 24–25; registry scan dated 2026-10-04. The O&M cliff is now a financing fact: the Bank was separately procuring "handholding" supervision at $0 disbursed while the state published no O&M budget (see ledgered WB-contract claims). PII note: registries were scrubbed before release; vendor fields are corporate, not personal. Upgrade path: AMC vendor + schedule via RTI.

claim: Every success or impact claim about RTFF & SDSS in the desk's media sweep is prospective ("can save lives", "expected to significantly reduce damage", "will predict"); no outlet in the swept corpus credits RTFF & SDSS or Chennai Flood Monitor for any warning during Cyclone Ditwah (30 Nov–6 Dec 2025) — credits go to IMD/RMC, CWC, district collectors and GCC's separate ICCC/EWS.
source: Desk media sweep register, 2026-10-03 (MEDIA-CLAIMS.md, entries 1–27 + pattern analysis)
notes: Documented absence within a dated, method-stated corpus (27 entries, sweep 2026-10-03). One chain only — our corpus — so not L4: Google/X indexing is partial and Tamil outlets (Dinamani, Daily Thanthi, Dinamalar, Hindu Tamil Thisai) are the thin layer; a second independent sweep of Tamil archives is the upgrade path. Negative findings from absence claims must always carry the corpus bounds.

claim: The predecessor portal chennaifloodsdss.in is NXDOMAIN (last Wayback capture 2025-08-31); only the desk's December-2023 rescue — 287 layers including 34,050 GCC zone-gauge readings (2020-11 → 2023-12, covering the full Michaung event) — survives as its record.
source: DNS/Wayback checks + desk rescue dataset chennai-rain-gauges (HF, pushed 2026-09-28)
notes: REPORT F9. Michaung datapoint inside the rescue: 639 mm in 24 h at a single GCC zone gauge (Zone 12, Meenambakkam 6A gate, 2023-12-04) — archived, reproducible by query on the chennai-rain-gauges dataset.
